commands_or_harness: before: sc_auth list-ctk-identities (kept only in a 0700 temp file + SHA-256 in memory; count recorded; stop if not empty); security list-smartcards (count only; stop if any); dscl . -read /Users/<user> AuthenticationAuthority (SHA-256 in memory only); sc_auth pairing_ui -s status

create: sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l heimdall-m00-p5-<16 hex> -k p-256-ne -t none (stdin /dev/null, timeout 20s); own hash = the single 40/64-hex token on the row(s) carrying the label; sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh -e b64 for the SSH hash
filter control: per load path a dedicated agent with KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES=<random non-matching hash>; ssh-add -s /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib and ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib; ssh-add -l

per load path: HOME=<tmp>/home-<path> KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES=<own hash> /usr/bin/ssh-agent -U -P /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib -a <tmp>/<path>.sock; every ssh tool runs with stdin /dev/null and SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force SSH_ASKPASS=/usr/bin/true (empty PIN, never a terminal prompt); ssh-add -s|-K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib; ssh-add -l/-L; ssh-add -T; ssh-keygen -Y sign -n heimdall-g04-p5 + -Y check-novalidate

login: ssh-keygen -s <fixture CA> -I heimdall-g04-p5-<run>-<path>-<variant> -n p-host1 -V -1m:+10m [-O no-touch-required, sk keys only, only after the default certificate was refused] <agent pubkey>; /usr/bin/ssh -F <tmp ssh_config> (ca1, IdentitiesOnly=yes, IdentityAgent=<dedicated>, ControlMaster=no, BatchMode=yes) true; controls: ca2 (principal mismatch) and ca1 with IdentityAgent=none; server lines from docker logs hm-m00t03-ca1 filtered to this run's key IDs
sampling: per sample and working path ssh-add -T, ssh-keygen -Y sign + check-novalidate, optional fresh ca1 login; ioreg IOConsoleLocked and CGSSessionScreenIsLocked only
export check: sc_auth export-ctk-identity -h <own hash> -f <tmp>/export.p12 -p <random, never recorded>; any file created is removed with rm -P

cleanup: kill exact agent PIDs; own-row check, then sc_auth delete-ctk-identity -h <own hash>; post-delete ssh-add -T / -Y sign on each working agent; sc_auth list-ctk-identities compared byte for byte (SHA-256) with the pre-run list; AuthenticationAuthority digest compared; rm -rf <tmp>

observed_result.criterion: Unlocked (screen stays unlocked), conjunction of clauses (observed_result.clauses): create_noninteractive = sc_auth creates the p-256-ne -t none CTK identity without timing out (stdin /dev/null, askpass answers empty); export_refused_no_file = export-ctk-identity creates no file and prints the hardware-bound refusal (its exit status, observed 0 on refusal, is recorded, not judged); delete_by_exact_hash_list_restored = delete-ctk-identity by the exact hash removes it and the identity list equals the pre-run list; dedicated_agent_signing = at least one /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib load path (PKCS#11 ssh-add -s, FIDO-style ssh-add -K -S) puts this run's key (ownership proven by EC-point hash or fingerprint) into a dedicated agent that signs (ssh-add -T, ssh-keygen -Y sign + check-novalidate) in every setup check and sample, and every path that loaded it does; keychain_certificates_limit = for every path that loaded the key, the same load with a random non-matching KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES loads zero keys; fixture_login_with_controls (only with --fixture-runtime) = a fresh certificate login to ca1 through the dedicated agent succeeds in setup and every sample while the ca2 principal-mismatch and ca1-without-agent controls are refused. Verdict pass if every applicable clause passes, fail if any clause fails. Validity: completed without interruption, a requested login was actually offered to the server, controls refused, identity list equal to the pre-run list, AuthenticationAuthority unchanged, agents and temp dir gone, no canary.
observed_result.summary: SELF-TEST with a fake sc_auth (no real token store, no ssh-keychain.dylib). mode=unlocked; identity created=yes (create_rc=0, timed_out=0); export_rc=0 export_file=absent (hardware_bounded_cannot_be_exported); deleted=yes; pkcs11: load_rc=0 keys=1 alg=ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 sign=available_all_samples login=available_all_samples login_class=accepted variant=default works=yes; sk: load_rc=0 keys=1 alg= sign=not_measured login=not_measured login_class= variant= works=no; samples=3; lock_window_evidence=not_applicable; identity_list_after_cleanup=matches_pre_run; cleanup_complete=true; canary_scan=clean.

sk.note: loaded key not confirmed as own; removed unused; raw output not kept

observed_result.server_logs: docker logs hm-m00t03-ca1 since run start, filtered to this run's key IDs and presence/touch lines (sshd-ca1-run-lines.log)
observed_result.findings: load path sk: the one loaded key could not be confirmed as this run's identity; removed unused;

limitations: One CTK identity in the real user token store (owner decision D4), created and deleted in this run. The owner's other identities are counted, never listed, exported, modified or used; the pre-run list stays in a 0700 temp file and as a digest in memory.
-t none only: no Touch ID per use. A -t bio identity, an exportable (p-256) identity, logout, sleep, reboot and headless (launchd) operation are not measured here.

The export password is random, single-use and protects nothing: sc_auth accepts it only as an argument, so it is visible to same-user processes while that one command runs. It is never written to logs, artifacts or this record.

No interactive prompt was answered by anyone: every command ran with stdin /dev/null, BatchMode and a timeout. A non-blocking notification (for example a SmartCard pairing offer) would not be visible to the probe; the AuthenticationAuthority digest check detects a pairing that was accepted.
ioreg IOConsoleLocked / CGSSessionScreenIsLocked are undocumented IORegistry properties used only as corroboration (lock mode).

Status verified means the measurement is valid (completed, cleanup complete including an identity list equal to the pre-run list); it holds even when the verdict is fail. Requirement IDs, where listed, are for traceability only (tests/evidence/README.md).
